newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Security on Tajik-Afghan border to be strengthened.
newsitem.headline: Security on Tajik-Afghan border to be strengthened.

text.p: Russian foreign minister Yevgeny Primakov and Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov agreed on Saturday to strengthen security along Tajikistan's border with Afghanistan, Russia's Interfax news agency said.
Primakov and Rakhmonov met in the Kazakh capital Almaty on Saturday, Interfax said, at the end of a Commonwealth of Independent States summit devoted to Afghanistan.
Leaders from Russia and four Central Asian republics at the summit agreed on Friday not to interfere in the Afghan conflict.

But, citing the Tajik president's spokesman, Zafar Sayidov, Interfax said Primakov and Rakhmonov had "agreed to take the necessary measures to strengthen security on the border between Tajikistan and Afghanistan". No details were given.

Russia already deploys thousands of border guards along the remote and mountainous border along the Amu Darya river. There are frequent clashes with Tajik Islamist guerrillas who cross over from bases inside Afghanistan to fight the Tajik government in the republic's own bloody four-year civil war.
